title: The Natty Arnold? (Joel Kellett aka Overkell)
summary: Lifter Profile episode on Joel Kellett (Overkell). He weighs the natty-or-not arguments (the facial changes are the most suspicious), then breaks down Joel's twice-a-day, six-days-a-week body-part split built on high volume and light weight, and grades his physique: elite chest and arms, a weak posterior chain and abs.
claims: Natty-or-not content is stupid; you should focus on your own training, not on what other people take
Joel is 6'1 and about 200 lb on stage at roughly 13-14% body fat; Arnold was 6'2 and 240-250 lb on stage and leaner, so the lean-mass gap is roughly 40 lb
A single freakishly developed muscle (Joel's chest, GVS's triceps) can come from great insertions plus obsessive training of that muscle rather than from drugs
Cheerleader effect: one outstanding muscle draws the eye and makes the weaker muscles around it look better; bodybuilding is a game of illusion
PED users usually have overgrown shoulders and traps because those muscles respond strongly to androgens; Joel's are underdeveloped next to his chest
Great skin and a full head of hair are weak but real signs against PED use
People who spend their time policing other men's PED use would be better off training hard for 10 years themselves
The strongest argument against Joel is his jaw and face growing noticeably from about age 26 to 32, which looks like growth hormone; diet does not explain it
More and more natural lifters seem to unlock new gains late in their careers by changing methods, almost a second round of newbie gains
Almost no natural lifter truly trains seriously for 10+ years, so nobody really knows what a fully trained natural looks like; Joel has trained seriously since about 20
Natural influencers who assume anyone bigger than them must be enhanced are thinking backwards; many of his viewers will end up bigger than he is
Natural YouTubers have nothing to sell (no supplements) and their only message is hard work, so being an influencer does not prove PED use
A natural who wants to promote natural lifting should not do business with known PED users
Pump, lighting and angle make people look enhanced; the same person looks ordinary standing in a shirt
Joel trains twice a day, six days a week, one muscle per session, each muscle twice a week, with 16-20+ sets per session, about 240 sets a week counting warm-ups; NH does about 110-120 sets a week
Two to three of every five sets Joel logs are warm-ups he counts, so his real working volume is roughly 16-20 hard sets per muscle per week
Joel uses light weights: about 15 lb for his top set of lateral raises and 90 lb for behind-the-head press
Hitting each muscle twice a week turns a body-part split from a bro split into a normal body-part split
After pull-ups and one pulldown variation the lats have had enough; more lat exercises are overkill, and you should add intensity instead of volume
He dislikes body-part splits because one muscle per day pushes you into junk volume to justify the trip to the gym
When you train twice a day it makes sense to have a day with no compounds, because you probably did upper-body compounds in the previous session
Supersets with no rest and constant drop sets artificially lower your performance and just pile up volume while fatigued, which he thinks is not best for hypertrophy
Joel's arm day is worth copying as is, minus one of the triceps movements
Joel says anything below 7-8 reps is strength training, not bodybuilding; NH disagrees, since naturals need the 6-10 and 4-8 ranges and the occasional 3x5
Every top natural NH knows trains heavy, intense and compound-focused; a light, isolation-heavy style like Joel's is how enhanced lifters typically train
Drop sets, cluster sets, tempo and short rests do raise intensity, but they should be the cherry on top, not the whole cake
Joel progresses by adding a set or rep here and there to build work capacity, and when a session gets to about two hours he splits it into two daily sessions
Joel and Arnold believe high-volume training leans out the muscle; NH is not convinced
Joel stays around 12-13% body fat and never does long cuts; spending half of every year dieting wastes years of potential progress
Joel sleeps 9-10 hours; recovery has to match training, not the other way round, and once-a-week training does too little damage to need much rest
Find a training method that fits your goals and life and that you enjoy; copying someone else will not work for you

Physique grades: chest S, biceps S, triceps long head S, shoulders A, quads A, neck A, teres A, lats B, lower and mid traps B, forearms B, abs C (a two-pack that he hides with vacuums), erectors, glutes and hamstrings C, calves poor
Golden Era aesthetics prioritised looking monstrous from the front, with chest and arms
Joel has almost no posterior chain because he skips hip hinges (no RDLs, good mornings or deadlifts), which Golden Era lifters avoided to keep the waist small
Influencers post only their best angles, which is why most of Joel's photos are from the front
You don't need to develop every muscle: push the muscles that serve your aesthetic goal very far, keep the rest maintained, and ignore people who shame you about skinny legs
